weights.weightCitation: Tokyo Guidelines TG18 (acute cholangitis/cholecystitis); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (Charcot's triad / Reynolds' pentad). Charcot's triad = RUQ pain + fever + jaundice; Reynolds' pentad adds confusion + hypotension (suppurative cholangitis — an emergency needing urgent biliary drainage + antibiotics).

Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (Courvoisier's law — painless jaundice + palpable gallbladder). PAINLESS progressive cholestatic jaundice + weight loss + pale stools/dark urine; Courvoisier — a painless palpable (non-tender) gallbladder suggests malignant obstruction (pancreatic head / cholangiocarcinoma) over stones.

AASLD & EASL Acute Liver Failure guidance; King's College criteria; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). Jaundice + ENCEPHALOPATHY + COAGULOPATHY (raised INR) within weeks, without pre-existing cirrhosis. UGANDA causes: HBV, hepatitis E (esp pregnancy), DILI (anti-TB, paracetamol, herbal). Paracetamol — King's College criteria + N-acetylcysteine; transfer for transplant assessment where available.

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on fever/malaria/sickle. UGANDA: holoendemic malaria — haemolytic (pre-hepatic) jaundice is common; jaundice in malaria is a SEVERITY marker needing IV artesunate; sickle-cell haemolytic crisis. TOKEN NUANCE: the combined 'Pale stools / dark urine' token argues AGAINST haemolysis — haemolysis gives DARK urine (haemoglobinuria) but NORMAL-coloured stools; only obstructive cholestasis gives PALE stools. A split dark-urine-only token would discriminate pre-hepatic from post-hepatic far better.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for Malaria (2025); ASH sickle-cell disease guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

WHO Hepatitis B & C guidelines; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). UGANDA: HEPATITIS B is endemic (high chronic carriage) and the dominant viral hepatitis; prodrome (fatigue, anorexia, nausea) then jaundice; check HBsAg / anti-HCV; distinguish acute HBV from a chronic-HBV flare. (Acute HAV/HEV — see Hepatitis A/E.)

AASLD/EASL alcohol-related liver disease guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). Jaundice as a marker of hepatic DECOMPENSATION — ascites (distension), variceal bleeding (haematemesis), encephalopathy, coagulopathy. In Uganda cirrhosis is often HBV ± alcohol; severe alcoholic hepatitis (Maddrey's) is a specific acute-on-chronic presentation.

Tokyo Guidelines TG18; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (choledocholithiasis). A common-bile-duct stone causes obstructive jaundice with COLICKY RUQ pain + pale stools/dark urine; added fever suggests superimposed cholangitis; PAINLESS progressive jaundice suggests malignancy instead.

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on HBV/liver disease/cancer. UGANDA: HCC is a LEADING cancer, driven by endemic HEPATITIS B — and notably can arise WITHOUT preceding cirrhosis in HBV and in YOUNGER patients than in the West. Presents late: RUQ mass + weight loss + decompensation. Undiagnosed HBV is common, so a LOW THRESHOLD for AFP + ultrasound is warranted even without a known liver-disease flag.
weights.weightCitation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines — HCC (Galle PR et al., 2018); WHO HBV/HCC guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on drug-exposed populations (anti-TB via 'tuberculosis'/'TB contact', ARVs via 'HIV', paracetamol). KEY TOKEN GAP: the actual DRUG HISTORY — anti-TB (isoniazid/rifampicin/pyrazinamide), ARVs (nevirapine/efavirenz), and especially TRADITIONAL/HERBAL medicines (extremely common in Uganda and a major cause of liver injury) — is NOT tokenised beyond 'paracetamol overdose'/'tuberculosis'. Recommend adding a current-medications + herbal/traditional-medicine field. Anti-TB hepatotoxicity needs drug interruption per WHO; paracetamol — King's College + NAC.
weights.weightCitation: AASLD/EASL DILI guidelines; WHO anti-TB hepatotoxicity guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.csoNote: UGANDA: amoebic liver abscess (Entamoeba histolytica) is COMMON — BUT jaundice is an UNCOMMON/MILD feature (it presents with RUQ pain + swinging fever + TENDER hepatomegaly, not prominent jaundice, unless a large abscess compresses the biliary tree). Included for the cholangitis overlap but weighted LOW for the jaundice complaint. Treatable with metronidazole; risk of rupture; serology/ultrasound.
weights.weightCitation: WHO amoebiasis guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (amoebic liver abscess)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on fever/exposure. WEIL'S disease = severe icteric leptospirosis (jaundice + ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY + bleeding + conjunctival suffusion + myalgia) — under-diagnosed in Uganda; rodent/water/flooding/farming exposure (only loosely 'high-risk exposure'). Treatable (penicillin/doxycycline). ACTIVE-OUTBREAK NOTE: in the current Bundibugyo Ebola PHEIC, febrile jaundice with BLEEDING + high-risk exposure within 21 days must ALSO trigger VHF precautions — isolate + notify (see the fever pack's VHF entry).
weights.weightCitation: WHO leptospirosis guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (Weil's disease)

weights.csoNote: Pre-hepatic HAEMOLYTIC jaundice: unconjugated bilirubin + pallor + DARK urine (haemoglobinuria) but NORMAL stool colour — so the combined 'Pale stools / dark urine' token misleads here too. G6PD deficiency (common in malaria-endemic Uganda; X-linked — males) causes episodic OXIDATIVE haemolysis triggered by oxidant DRUGS (primaquine/dapsone/sulfonamides), fava beans, or infection — the oxidant-drug trigger is not tokenised. Also covers autoimmune/other haemolysis.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022); WHO G6PD deficiency guidance

weights.csoNote: Acute faeco-oral (HAV) / waterborne (HEV) viral hepatitis — common with poor sanitation in Uganda and OUTBREAK-PRONE (HEV genotype 1 circulates in East Africa, esp refugee/displaced settings). Usually self-limiting BUT hepatitis E is SEVERE/FULMINANT IN PREGNANCY (high mortality — escalate to the Acute Liver Failure entry). Contaminated-water/sanitation exposure is only loosely captured as 'high-risk exposure'.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Hepatitis A & E guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

weights.csoNote: IMPORTANT TEACHING: hepatic/intestinal schistosomiasis (S. mansoni — common around Lake Victoria/Albert) causes Symmers' PERIPORTAL FIBROSIS → PRESINUSOIDAL PORTAL HYPERTENSION (splenomegaly, oesophageal varices → haematemesis) with PRESERVED hepatocellular function — so it characteristically does NOT cause jaundice. JAUNDICE in a schistosomiasis patient should prompt a search for a CONCURRENT cause (viral hepatitis, HCC, decompensation). Marked less_likely for the jaundice complaint deliberately; freshwater-contact exposure only loosely 'high-risk exposure'.
weights.weightCitation: WHO schistosomiasis guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (Symmers' periportal fibrosis)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on fever. Web-verified: UGANDA is in the YELLOW FEVER belt with RECURRENT outbreaks (annual suspected cases; recent outbreaks incl. Buikwe/Buvuma and Ngora; a national vaccination campaign is ongoing but coverage is INCOMPLETE — ~123/146 districts). Severe YF = febrile jaundice + bleeding + hepatorenal failure; a NOTIFIABLE outbreak disease — notify public health. Vaccination status and forest/mosquito exposure are not well tokenised. Overlaps the VHF picture — in the current Bundibugyo Ebola PHEIC, febrile jaundice with bleeding + high-risk exposure within 21 days must trigger VHF precautions: isolate + notify.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Yellow Fever guidance; Uganda MoH / WHO Uganda yellow-fever reports (2024-2026, web-verified); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)
